description: The bar charts illustrate the accuracy percentages for different methods on the PHEME and PolitiFact datasets, with each chart displaying six bars corresponding to the categories: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition,' arranged along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%)', employs a linear scale ranging from 75.0 to 95.0 with tick intervals of 2.5%. In the PHEME chart, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at 89.84%, followed by 'w/o select' at 88.80%, 'w/o emotion' at 87.34%, and 'w/o cognition' at 87.17%; the 'w/o comments' method scores 86.82%, while the 'w/o text' method shows the lowest accuracy at 80.10%. In the PolitiFact chart, the 'Ours' method again achieves the highest accuracy at 90.57%, followed by 'w/o select' at 89.62%, 'w/o cognition' at 87.74%, 'w/o emotion' at 84.91%, 'w/o comments' at 85.85%, and 'w/o text' at 83.02%. The bars are colored distinctly—'Ours' is dark red, 'w/o comments' is orange, 'w/o text' is pale yellow, 'w/o select' is light blue, 'w/o emotion' is medium blue, and 'w/o cognition' is dark blue—and are not sorted, appearing in the order listed on the horizontal axis. No bars are visually emphasized or annotated beyond their labeled values.
caption_used: The bar charts illustrate the accuracy percentages for different methods on the PHEME and PolitiFact datasets. Each chart contains six bars representing the categories: 'Ours,' 'w/o comments,' 'w/o text,' 'w/o select,' 'w/o emotion,' and 'w/o cognition,' placed along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis, labeled 'Accuracy (%),' uses a linear scale ranging from 75% to 95% with tick intervals of 2.5%. In the PHEME chart, the 'Ours' method achieves the highest accuracy at approximately 89.84%, followed closely by 'w/o select' at 89.80%. The 'w/o text' method shows a significant decline, reaching only 75.10%, the lowest value in the dataset. In the PolitiFact chart, the 'Ours' method again demonstrates the highest accuracy at 90.57%, while 'w/o comments' and 'w/o cognition' exhibit similar performance at 85.85% and 85.74%, respectively. The results suggest that removing text features has the most detrimental impact on accuracy, while the exclusion of comments and cognition leads to comparable performance levels across both datasets.
